scope: Application-level Outbox/Inbox owner fencing and lease takeover matrix against an isolated real MySQL 8.4.11 sandbox

git.worktree_state: dirty; pre-existing and task-related changes were preserved and not committed

environment.isolation: isolated Docker container; dedicated sandbox database; no production connection

schema_baseline.type: minimal migration dependency chain; not a full V1-to-V120 production baseline

execution.command: SPRING_DATASOURCE_URL=<redacted>; SPRING_DATASOURCE_USERNAME=root; SPRING_DATASOURCE_PASSWORD=<redacted>; mvn -pl zhicloud-server -am test -Dtest=EventOwnerFencingMysqlIntegrationTest -Dsurefire.failIfNoSpecifiedTests=false -Dzhicloud.mysql.integration=true
verified_behaviors: Active Inbox lease returns IN_PROGRESS and does not execute the handler.
Expired Inbox lease can be taken over and settled as PROCESSED.
A stale Inbox owner cannot settle success after takeover; settlement fails closed.
Inbox handler failure marks FAILED, increments retry_count, clears owner/lease, and records the error.
Eight concurrent first deliveries execute the Inbox handler exactly once; one result is PROCESSED and the other seven are IN_PROGRESS before winner settlement.
An active Outbox lease blocks a second claim; after expiry a new owner can take over.
A stale Outbox owner cannot markPublished or markRetry after takeover; the new owner and PUBLISHING state remain intact.
A stale Outbox owner cannot mark dead after takeover; the new owner can subsequently mark dead.
Eight concurrent Outbox claim calls produce exactly one winner.

diagnostic_notes: The first matrix invocation failed before test execution because PowerShell-to-mvn.cmd argument parsing split Maven options; it is not application or MySQL semantic evidence.

The first real-MySQL matrix execution exposed two test harness defects: the concurrency test waited on the blocked winner before releasing it, and the stale-owner assertion incorrectly expected an actively leased PUBLISHING row to be returned by selectClaimable. Both were corrected; the passing run above is the evidence run.

proven: Real MySQL 8.4.11 application-level Inbox and Outbox owner fencing semantics.
Real MySQL row-level CAS behavior for concurrent Inbox first delivery and Outbox claim.
Lease expiry takeover and stale-owner fail-closed settlement behavior in the tested single-node sandbox.
not_covered: Real read/write splitting or multi-tenant dynamic datasource topology.
Network partition and process crash/failover injection.
End-to-end Outbox publish, DLQ, replay, compensation, and reconciliation workflows.
Production data volume, latency, lock contention, long-running migration, and independent review.

limits: This is sandbox evidence and cannot be represented as production validation.
The database was a dedicated sandbox database in a single-node Docker container.
The schema baseline was a minimal dependency chain, not the complete production migration baseline.
The test does not validate physical replication, failover, or production-scale behavior.

reproducibility.prerequisite: Use the dedicated zhicloud_sandbox_chain database on the existing isolated MySQL sandbox container; do not use production credentials or databases.
reproducibility.secret_handling: The database password is intentionally omitted and must be injected through SPRING_DATASOURCE_PASSWORD at execution time.
notes: Run from the repository root with PowerShell.
Do not put the JDBC URL with query parameters directly on the mvn.cmd command line because cmd.exe treats ampersands as command separators.
The migration chain is minimal and does not establish the full production migration baseline.
